notes: GeoSN historical orthophoto capture year 2012 identifies paved centerlines independently. The manufacturer identifies separately usable 3.7 km and 2.2 km courses and configurable training sections. The comparison shapes show alternatives, so named branch paths preserve each configuration set rather than asserting one timed lap. Later dynamic-course additions are excluded. Historical direction, lap choice and present-day corner alignment remain unverified. Independently digitized aerial branch network: 2713.9 m. Shared edges count once; this configuration set is not a single lap, and no line joins separate paths. Direction, historical configuration and fine corner alignment remain draft; no course coordinates come from the comparison catalogue.

sources.notes: Road surfaces are triangulated directly between this layout's saved border rings. Elevation follows the approximately 78 m terrain raster, not a survey of the road. Curbs are geometry-based illustrations on curved boundaries; their locations, widths, heights and colours are assumed, not extracted from imagery. Banking is unknown. The source is an open route or branch network, without one validated closed driving order. Lap playback is unavailable. Boundary coordinates and their separate feature-level licence are preserved. Imagery loads externally on demand; no image bytes or meshes are stored.

imagery.attribution: GeoSN, dl-de/by-2-0; historical DOP 2012–2014, capture year 2012. Original source slices interpreted as paved perimeter and six grass islands; ideal branch paths calculated.

networkReview.note: The pinned 2012 GeoSN image supports an unchanged outer pavement perimeter and six separate grass islands assembled from exact original boundary slices. Saved contours stitch across paved junctions and duplicate parts of adjoining edges. Every source vertex is accounted for; omitted junction duplicates, pavement stitches and one near-return paint spur are listed explicitly. New joins are at most 2 m, or at most 60 m and within a 0.1 m capsule of an existing source segment. The source branches, original GeoJSON boundaries, timing and terrain remain unchanged. The closed source branch crosses itself at the western paved junction; its calculated path preserves that crossing and visit order instead of deleting a route section. The two alternatives stay open and disconnected. Native image, full overlays and local junctions were reviewed. This is a 2D estimated pavement interpretation, not a unique timed lap, present-day course qualification or surveyed edge measurement.
